title: Superpolynomial \(\mathrm{AC}^{0}[p]\)-Frege lower bounds
formal:
For every prime integer \(p\), does there exist a single polynomial-time constructible family of DNF tautologies \((\tau_{p,n})_{n\ge1}\) of length polynomially related to \(n\), such that its proofs in the fixed modular Frege calculus below exceed every polynomial size bound at every fixed line depth? Precisely, require for each \(p\) a finite deterministic machine \(M_p\) and integers \(C_p,k_p\ge1\) such that, for every \(n\ge1\), on input \(1^n\) the machine outputs a DNF \(\tau_{p,n}\) within \(C_p(n+2)^{k_p}\) bit steps, this formula is a tautology, and
\[n\le |\tau_{p,n}|\le C_p(n+2)^{k_p}.\]
The required lower bound is
\[\forall d,r,N\in\mathbb{N}_{\ge1}\ \exists n\ge N\ \forall\pi\;\bigl(\operatorname{Proof}_{p,d}(\pi,\tau_{p,n})\Rightarrow |\pi|>n^r\bigr).\]
The machine and the family may depend on \(p\) but not on \(d,r,N\); the witness \(n\) may depend on all three. No effective procedure producing \(M_p\) from \(p\) is required. The family consists of genuine tautologies, not formulas whose lack of short proofs might be due to falsity. The lower bound is infinitely often, not necessarily eventually for every \(n\).
definitions:
Fix a prime \(p\ge2\). Formulas are finite ordered syntax trees built from constants \(0,1\), variables \(x_i\) for \(i\in\mathbb{N}=\{0,1,\ldots\}\), unary \(\neg\), binary \(\land,\lor\), and gates \(\operatorname{MOD}_{p,j}(A_1,\ldots,A_t)\) for \(0\le j<p\) and any finite arity \(t\ge0\). Under an assignment of Boolean values to the variables, the usual connectives have their ordinary truth tables, and a modular gate is true exactly when the number of its true arguments is congruent to \(j\) modulo \(p\). A tautology is true under every assignment. A literal is a variable or its negation. A DNF is a finite disjunction of finite conjunctions of literals, written as a binary formula with any parenthesization; an empty conjunction is \(1\), an empty disjunction is \(0\), and a singleton conjunction or disjunction is its sole member. Target DNFs contain no modular gates.

The notation \(A\Rightarrow B\) is an abbreviation for \(\neg A\lor B\), and \(A\Leftrightarrow B\) abbreviates \((A\Rightarrow B)\land(B\Rightarrow A)\). Both are expanded fully before checking syntax, depth or size. Fix the following finite ordinary Frege axiom schemes, in the order displayed:
\[\begin{gathered}
 A\Rightarrow(B\Rightarrow A),\\
 (A\Rightarrow(B\Rightarrow C))\Rightarrow((A\Rightarrow B)\Rightarrow(A\Rightarrow C)),\\
 (\neg B\Rightarrow\neg A)\Rightarrow(A\Rightarrow B),\\
 (A\land B)\Rightarrow A,\qquad (A\land B)\Rightarrow B,\\
 A\Rightarrow(B\Rightarrow(A\land B)),\\
 A\Rightarrow(A\lor B),\qquad B\Rightarrow(A\lor B),\\
 (A\Rightarrow C)\Rightarrow((B\Rightarrow C)\Rightarrow((A\lor B)\Rightarrow C)),\\
 1,\qquad \neg0.
\end{gathered}\]
The metavariables \(A,B,C\) may be replaced consistently by arbitrary formulas of the full modular language. The sole inference rule is modus ponens: from earlier lines \(A\) and \(A\Rightarrow B\), infer \(B\). There are no hypotheses. Besides these eleven schemes, allow the modular axioms
\[\operatorname{MOD}_{p,0}(),\qquad \neg\operatorname{MOD}_{p,j}()\quad(1\le j<p),\]
and every instance of
\[\operatorname{MOD}_{p,j}(\Gamma,A)\Leftrightarrow
 \bigl((\operatorname{MOD}_{p,j}(\Gamma)\land\neg A)\lor
 (\operatorname{MOD}_{p,j-1}(\Gamma)\land A)\bigr),\]
where \(\Gamma\) is any finite ordered list of formulas, including the empty list, and \(j-1\) is reduced modulo \(p\) to \(\{0,\ldots,p-1\}\). These are the modular schemes of the cited source, attached to the specified finite complete classical Frege basis. An axiom line must match its indicated scheme syntactically after expansion, using the same substituted formula at each occurrence of a metavariable. A proof is a nonempty finite sequence of axiom or modus-ponens lines ending with the claimed formula. Earlier lines may be reused without restriction. There are no extension-variable definition axioms, no separate substitution rule for previously derived lines, and no restrictions of regularity or tree shape.

Define the logical depth \(\delta\) of constants and variables to be zero. Negation has depth \(1+\delta(A)\), and a modular gate has depth \(1+\max(0,\delta(A_1),\ldots,\delta(A_t))\). For a conjunction, flatten its maximal connected subtree of conjunction nodes and collect the boundary subformulas whose roots are not conjunctions; its depth is one plus the maximum depth of those subformulas. Use the same rule for disjunctions. Flattening does not cross a negation, modular gate or different Boolean connective. It defines the depth measure only: the actual binary syntax tree is still written and counted in full. A depth-at-most-\(d\) proof must have \(\delta\le d\) for every line, including instantiated axioms and the conclusion. This bounds individual formulas, not the length of an inference path in the proof graph. Such paths and the total number of lines are unrestricted.

All sizes are bits in a fixed prefix encoding. For \(t\ge0\), let \(b(t)\) be its binary expansion without leading zeros, with \(b(0)=0\), and let \(E(t)=1^{|b(t)|}0b(t)\), using concatenation. Formula tags 000 and 001 encode constants \(0\) and \(1\); 010 followed by \(E(i)\) encodes \(x_i\); 011 followed by the child encodes negation; 100 and 101 followed by both child encodings encode conjunction and disjunction. Tag 110 followed by \(E(j)E(t)\) and all \(t\) ordered child encodings represents \(\operatorname{MOD}_{p,j}\). Tag 111 is invalid. The prime is fixed by the system, not supplied as an oracle. A proof starts with \(E(m)\), its positive number of lines. Each line contains \(E(q)\) followed by its complete formula encoding. Rule labels \(q=1,\ldots,11\) refer to the ordinary schemes in their displayed order; labels 12, 13 and 14 refer respectively to the empty-zero-residue, empty-nonzero-residue and recursive modular schemes. Label 15 denotes modus ponens and is followed, after the formula, by \(E(a)E(b)\): on line \(j\), require \(1\le a,b<j\), line \(a=A\) and line \(b=A\Rightarrow B\), with the current line exactly \(B\). Other rule labels and malformed strings are invalid. The length \(|\pi|\) includes every variable index, gate, repeated formula occurrence, line count and inference reference. Formula length uses the same formula encoding. Nothing is given by a compressed circuit, advice or a program for generating a larger proof.

The predicate \(\operatorname{Proof}_{p,d}(\pi,\tau)\) means validity under all these rules, conclusion \(\tau\), and line depth at most \(d\). Construction time for the target family is measured on a standard deterministic Turing machine with a fixed finite number of tapes and a finite alphabet containing input/output bits and blank. A transition reads and writes at most one cell per tape and moves each head by at most one cell; all transitions and output writes count. Each \(M_p\) is one finite program, with no oracle or length-dependent advice. Its constants \(C_p,k_p\) may depend on that program and the fixed prime. The formula-size lower bound \(|\tau_{p,n}|\ge n\) and polynomial upper bound make size in \(n\) polynomially comparable with size in the conclusion. Quantifying over positive integer exponents \(r\) is equivalent to exceeding every polynomial bound, including bounds with arbitrary fixed multiplicative constants.
answer_criterion: Supply the stated families, their construction machines and bounds, together with a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean that all outputs are DNF tautologies and that the displayed lower-bound quantifiers hold for every prime and every fixed line depth. Alternatively, give a complete Lean proof of the logical negation: some prime \(p\) has no family satisfying all the stated requirements. Equivalently, for that prime, every polynomial-time constructible DNF tautology family of the prescribed length scale has some fixed depth \(d\), exponent \(r\) and threshold \(N\) for which every \(n\ge N\) admits a valid depth-\(d\) proof of size at most \(n^r\). A negative answer does not require an efficient proof-finding algorithm. Unproved tautologicity, one fixed polynomial lower bound, a bound only at restricted derivation depth, or a result for only one prime does not establish the full positive claim. All assumptions, construction bounds, depth and size conventions must match the card. This binary asymptotic claim retains its polynomial precision; the numerical 1/100 tolerance is not a replacement for a proof-size lower bound.
why: This is a central unresolved comparison between the expressive power of shallow formulas and the length of rigorous deductions. Ordinary bounded-depth Frege lower bounds are known, but modular gates permit compact reasoning about arithmetic counts, including parity. Proving the stated lower bounds would move a major proof-complexity frontier beyond shallow reasoning without modular counting.

importance.reason: A classical next step beyond the strongest broadly established bounded-depth Frege lower bounds, with direct connections to algebraic proof systems and a persistent gap between circuit and proof complexity.

progress.text: Ajtai establishes superpolynomial ordinary bounded-depth Frege lower bounds for pigeonhole formulas; Pitassi, Beame and Impagliazzo publish exponential-type improvements in 1993. These systems do not contain modular gates.

Krajíček gives the explicit modular Frege schemes and flattened logical-depth convention in §5 of the preprint, revised 27 September 2023 and published in November 2024. The modular lower-bound frontier remains open there.
Efremenko and Itsykson publish tree-like lifting and stronger size-versus-derivation-depth tradeoffs for resolution over parities. Derivation depth is not the logical depth of each line.
Lu, Santhanam and Tzameret publish an unconditional no-short-proof result for explicit candidate DNFs while leaving their tautologicity unresolved. The full arXiv version is v1 of 20 September 2025.
Itsykson, Podolskii and Shekhovtsov report near-quadratic derivation-depth lifting and an unconditional quadratic size lower bound for parity resolution, under their stated lifting conditions.

Hakoniemi, Limaye and Tzameret publish ECCC TR26-070, submitted 5 May, reporting hard Boolean CNF instances for the restricted linear-certificate roABP fragment of IPS, for all variable orders and fields.

status_note: Explicitly open in Krajíček’s 2023/2024 source and the checked 2025/2026 primary literature. Bounded checks through 15 September 2026 did not identify a resolution of the retained uniform DNF-family target for every fixed prime. The ITCS 2026 candidate DNFs still have unproved tautologicity in the listed full version; the checked ECCC results restrict derivation depth, give polynomial size bounds, or restrict algebraic certificates. These checks do not independently certify all new proofs or exhaust the literature.

context_blocks.text: A modular gate states that a count has a particular residue. The case \(p=2\) includes parity, while other primes give other fixed modular tests. A bounded-depth proof may make arbitrarily many deductions, each of which uses only a bounded number of logical layers. Krajíček's §5 explicitly defines the modular recurrence axioms and the depth convention that flattens consecutive conjunctions or disjunctions. The card fixes a finite ordinary basis and a complete binary encoding within that presentation.

The saved benchmark asks for one efficiently generated DNF family for each prime that defeats all fixed line depths, with the same family at every exponent. This explicit construction and quantifier order are retained as the card's chosen formulation of the broad modular-Frege frontier; they are not silently replaced by a family chosen separately for each depth. A method for selecting the program uniformly from the prime is not an additional requirement. Hard instances may occur on different infinite subsequences at different depths and exponents.

Without modular gates, the bounded-depth comparison has established lower bounds. Ajtai's 1988 work proves superpolynomial bounds for propositional pigeonhole formulas, and Pitassi, Beame and Impagliazzo's 1993 paper strengthens them to exponential-type size bounds at each fixed depth. These are statements about ordinary bounded-depth Frege. Adding all modular axiom instances enlarges the set of possible proofs, so an ordinary-Frege lower bound does not itself establish the present one.

Circuit lower bounds and proof lower bounds measure different things. Prime-modulus circuit lower bounds concern nonconstant Boolean functions that cannot be computed by small circuits. Every tautology in this card instead computes the constant true function. The object required to be large is a syntactically verified deduction of that tautology in a fixed calculus. The February 2026 source explicitly retains modular Frege lower bounds as open while distinguishing the circuit results.

Resolution over parities permits disjunctions of linear equations modulo two as proof lines. It is a restricted proof system within the modular-Frege setting. Efremenko and Itsykson's CCC 2025 Theorems 3 and 4 give a tree-like lifting statement and a size-versus-derivation-depth tradeoff, respectively. For their lifted Tseitin family with \(m\) variables, the latter requires either size \(2^{\Omega(m/\log m)}\) or derivation depth \(\Omega(m\log m)\). These results leave open proofs of polynomial size with sufficiently long inference paths; the present card permits such paths.

Itsykson, Podolskii and Shekhovtsov's February 2026 result gives a stronger tradeoff for parity resolution. After the specified fixed-gadget lifting, resolution width \(w\) of the original CNF forces derivation depth \(\Omega(w^2/\log S)\) in a size-\(S\) parity-resolution refutation, and also an unconditional size bound \(\Omega(w^2)\). Here width is the maximum number of literals in a clause, minimized over ordinary resolution refutations. The construction and gadget conditions remain part of the source theorem. The depth tradeoff and quadratic bound each fall short of a superpolynomial bound on unrestricted derivation size.

Lu, Santhanam and Tzameret's full version states in Corollary 5.7 that, for every prime, an explicit DNF sequence has no polynomial-size modular Frege proofs. Crucially, the same corollary describes the formulas' validity as unknown. A false formula has no proof in a sound calculus, so lack of short proofs alone cannot certify a hard tautology. The ITCS 2026 published abstract retains this distinction and discusses conditional evidence for tautologicity. Those conditions have not become unconditional theorems in the versions checked here.

Hakoniemi, Limaye and Tzameret's May 2026 report states exponential-type lower bounds for actual Boolean CNF instances in \(\mathrm{roABP}\text{-}\mathrm{IPS}_{\mathrm{LIN}}\), where the algebraic certificate representation is restricted to read-once oblivious algebraic branching programs in the linear-certificate model. The stated bound holds for every variable order and every field. It is stronger in instance scope than earlier purely algebraic examples, but it retains its restriction on certificate representation. It therefore does not supply lower bounds against arbitrary modular-Frege deductions. The report's new complete proof was not independently verified in this card review.

The target excludes hardness arising merely from an enormous conclusion or an unbounded search for its description: every output has polynomial length and a polynomial-time construction, and its truth must be proved. It also excludes confusing a fixed bound such as \(n^{10}\) with growth beyond every polynomial. The depth, prime and uniform-family conventions are part of the mathematical question rather than implementation details that can be decided after submitting a proof.

sentences: Modular Frege proofs can reason with shallow Boolean formulas containing gates that count true inputs modulo a fixed prime.
The problem asks for one polynomial-time constructible DNF tautology family per prime that requires superpolynomial total proof size at every fixed logical line depth.
The statement fixes a complete finite classical calculus, the modular recurrence axioms, all encodings and the distinction between formula depth and unrestricted derivation depth.
Ordinary bounded-depth lower bounds and recent parity-resolution or restricted algebraic results do not establish this stronger modular-Frege target.
A complete Lean proof must supply genuine tautologies and all construction and lower-bound guarantees, or prove the logical negation of the specified family-existence claim.
